doc.title: Jimmy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Composing process and computers
summary: Heath explains how he uses the computer and notation software and gets ideas at the piano and saxophone, as Dizzy advised.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Can you talk a little bit about your process when you’re composing? How do you write? Do you use a computer for anything?

I use a computer for everything now, except to get ideas together. To format everything I’ve been on the computer since I started teaching at Queens, ’86 or ’87, that’s when I got my first computer and got my first notation program. Now it’s really advanced, a program called Finale. Well, I get ideas together by playing on the piano, which Dizzy told me to do many years ago, “If you’re going to write some music man, you got to play the keyboard.” I get things together, harmonically, on the keyboard. I play my saxophone and get melody, ideas, and sing melodies to myself. There’s so many different ways that music is revealed to you.
